clue.text: Big tree outside university

indicators.note: the tree is said to stand outside the university, so it wraps round its letter

parts.note: a poplar is a tall tree

explanation.surface: A huge tree stands just beyond the university grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something popular is a big hit, widely liked, as in 'a big name'.

clue.text: Become confused following parking — beginning of spousal rows

indicators.note: the confusion word comes after the parking letter

parts.note: to addle is to become muddled

indicators.note: the first letter of the word spousal is taken

explanation.surface: A couple get muddled while parking, which starts their marital rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' looks like quarrels from the surface, but it is the verb: paddles a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To paddle a canoe is to row it, both verbs in the third person.

clue.text: Applauded after pressure's lifted

indicators.note: the lifted word comes after the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure
raised means lifted

explanation.surface: Relief and applause once the pressure has been lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: Praised means commended, applauded, both past tense.

clue.text: Spanking ne'er-do-well's rear with awful rage

indicators.note: the rear of the word is its final letter
an awful version of the letters of rage is a jumble of them

explanation.surface: A scoundrel gets a spanking on the backside in a terrible fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear' gives L, the last letter of NE'ER-DO-WELL; 'awful' turns RAGE into ARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanking in informal use means impressively big, as in a spanking great house.

clue.text: Rest cue having pocketed second of balls

indicators.note: the cue word holds the letter in its pocket, so it goes inside

parts.note: a cue is a prompt, a reminder

indicators.note: the second letter of the word balls is taken

explanation.surface: A snooker cue that has pocketed one ball now rests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cue' and 'pocketed' paint snooker, but a cue here is a prompt.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left, the rest.

clue.text: Selects chess moves, pressing centre of clock twice

indicators.note: one piece is pressed into the other, so it sits inside it
the letters of the word chess are moved about into a new order
the centre letter is to be used two times over
the middle letter of the word clock is taken

explanation.surface: A chess player makes moves, slapping the clock in the middle of the game twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' and 'clock' make you think of a chess game, but 'moves' is the anagram signal giving CHSES, and 'pressing' pushes the doubled middle letter into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose is to select, both verbs in the third person.

clue.text: Stick chlorine in bottom of jug

parts.note: Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine

indicators.note: the bottom of a down entry word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Chlorine residue sticks to the base of a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to stick fast, both verbs.

clue.text: 'Possession' wins her 'top novel' — not Byatt's last

indicators.note: a novel arrangement of these letters is a new one
the letter named after this is excluded from the pool
the final letter of Byatt is taken

explanation.surface: A. S. Byatt's 'Possession' wins first prize as the best novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges WINSHERTOP minus T, the last letter of BYATT; 'Possession' is also the Booker-winning Byatt novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership means having possession of something.

clue.text: Throttle lever initially missing? Bizarre

indicators.note: the named letter is missing from the throttling word

parts.note: to throttle is to strangle

indicators.note: the first letter of the word lever is taken

explanation.surface: A machine's throttle lever is oddly missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops L, the first letter of LEVER, from STRANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange means odd, bizarre, both adjectives.

clue.text: Some rockets send astronauts the wrong way, creating misery

indicators.note: the run is read the wrong way, from right to left
only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: Rockets sending astronauts in the wrong direction cause despair.
explanation.walkthrough: The run SSENDAS sits across rocketS SEND ASTronauts; 'the wrong way' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadness is unhappiness, so misery is a near synonym.

clue.text: A grid fabricated by a male — it's designed to explain something

indicators.note: something fabricated is made up, so the letters are made up afresh

explanation.surface: A man has built a grid of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabricated' rearranges A GRID into DIAGR, then A and M follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a drawing whose purpose is to explain how something works.

clue.text: Took no notice of tailor ordering no end of fur

indicators.note: to tailor is to alter and refashion, so these letters are reworked
the letter named next is to be absent from the rearranged pool
the final letter of the word fur is taken

explanation.surface: Someone ignored a tailor's instruction to stop using fur trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailor' rearranges ORDERING, but 'no end of fur' says the R (last letter of FUR) is left out of the pool, leaving seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to take no notice of it, both in the past tense.

clue.text: Hearing what a ship might be doing around ends of the haven

indicators.note: the ship's activity goes around the letters taken from the haven

parts.words: what a ship might be doing
parts.note: a damaged ship may be listing, leaning to one side

indicators.note: the last letters of the words the and haven are taken

explanation.surface: A harbour watcher wonders what a ship is up to near the harbour mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends of the haven' gives E and N, the last letters of THE and HAVEN, placed inside LISTING by 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing, as a present participle, means paying attention with the ears.

clue.text: Fury surrounding new kitchen fireplace

indicators.note: the anger word goes round the letter for new, enclosing it

parts.note: fury is rage

explanation.surface: Anger erupts over a brand-new kitchen fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is an old cast-iron cooking stove set in a kitchen hearth.

clue.text: Secretive about promotion, unfortunately

indicators.note: the secretive word goes about, around, the promotion word

parts.note: sly means secretive, cunning
an ad promotes a product

explanation.surface: Someone sadly keeps quiet about their job promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadly used as a sentence adverb means regrettably or alas.

clue.text: Canadian rock star disturbed rest for child

parts.note: Neil Young is a Canadian rock musician

indicators.note: the letters of rest are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A Canadian rocker's sleep is disturbed by a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges REST into STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster is a young person, a child.

clue.text: District Attorney, with an exclamation of repugnance, meeting majority of brusque relations

parts.note: DA is the American abbreviation for District Attorney
ugh is what you say in disgust

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, dropping its last letter

parts.note: terse means brusque, curt

explanation.surface: A prosecutor, disgusted, confronts some curt relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority of' drops the final E of TERSE to give TERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Daughters are family members, so they are relations.

clue.text: Nude worried by start of Rubenesque wrinkle, causing stress

indicators.note: worried letters are shaken about into a new order
the first letter of the word Rubenesque is taken

parts.note: a line on the face is a wrinkle

explanation.surface: A nude model frets over a wrinkle on a Rubens-style figure, which is stressful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges NUDE into UNDE; 'causing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline a point is to emphasise or stress it.

clue.text: Overwhelmed, prisoner asked one to leave

parts.note: con is slang for a convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: the letter for one departs from the asking word

parts.note: queried means asked
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prisoner, overwhelmed, has been asked to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes I from QUERIED, giving QUERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Conquered means defeated, overcome, so overwhelmed.

clue.text: Cut-up artwork with article rejected for Eastern educational establishment

indicators.note: one letter is thrown out and another put in its place

parts.note: a collage is art made from cut-up pieces stuck together
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A collage artwork is turned down by an Eastern college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected for' swaps the A in COLLAGE for E.
explanation.definitionFit: A college is a place of further or higher education.

clue.text: Securing number below par

parts.note: ailing means unwell, feeling below par

explanation.surface: A golfer secures a score one under par.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below par' suggests golf scores but means unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailing something down means securing it, fastening it firmly.

clue.text: Whiffs pants

definitions.meaning: whiffs as a noun means small gusts of smoke or smell
pants as a verb means breathes in short gasps

explanation.definitionFit: Puffs are brief breaths of air or smoke, and to puff is to pant.

clue.text: Catastrophe if a rule's broken

indicators.note: broken letters are smashed and put back together differently

parts.note: the 's is the possessive, giving no letter

explanation.surface: Breaking a rule leads to disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges IFARULE.
explanation.definitionFit: A failure is a fiasco or disaster, so a catastrophe.

clue.text: Recommend last bit of grog's swallowed by drunk guests

indicators.note: the letter is swallowed, so it sits inside the other piece
drunk letters stagger into a new order
the final letter of grog is taken

explanation.surface: Tipsy guests down the last drop of grog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges GUESTS into SUGEST, and G, the last letter of GROG, goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest something is to put it forward, recommend it.

clue.text: Fish caught in beginning of year? On the contrary — whoppers being invented

indicators.note: one piece is caught inside the other
this reverses the stated order, so the fish holds the year's letter instead

parts.note: a ling is a sea fish of the cod family

indicators.note: the first letter of the word year is taken

explanation.surface: An angler claims a fish was caught at New Year, but those are tall tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, the fish goes inside Y; 'On the contrary' flips that, so Y goes inside LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying is telling falsehoods; whoppers are big lies, so inventing them is lying.

clue.text: Temporarily having hygiene problem with last bit of hair falling out

parts.note: BO is body odour

indicators.note: the final letter of the word hair is taken

parts.note: rowing means quarrelling, falling out

explanation.surface: Someone with a hygiene problem is losing the last of their hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling out' looks like hair loss but means quarrelling, ROWING (rhymes with 'cowing').
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowing something means having it for a while before giving it back.

clue.text: Man with no hair left moving slightly poorly

indicators.note: one letter shifts by a single position within the word

parts.note: a baldy is a bald man

explanation.surface: A balding man is moving a little unsteadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving slightly' shifts the L in BALDY one place along.
explanation.definitionFit: Badly means poorly, in a bad way, both adverbs.

clue.text: Turn up once, oddly, with dog

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word once are taken

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Once in a while a stray dog shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives O and C from ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur is to happen or arise, to turn up.

clue.text: Was present left to absorb son?

indicators.note: the leaving word takes in the son's letter, enclosing it

parts.note: exited means left, went out

explanation.surface: A question of whether someone departed and took their son along.
explanation.definitionFit: Existed means was there, was in being, a past-tense match for was present.

clue.text: At home, hint about diamonds to get embrace

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the hint word goes about, around, the diamonds letter

parts.note: a clue is a hint
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: At home, a partner drops hints about diamonds to win a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace a thing is to take it in, so include is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Enthusiastically changing gear in city

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the city name

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

indicators.note: changing the letters of gear gives a new order

explanation.surface: A driver keenly changes gear in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing gear' reads like driving, but 'changing' is the anagram signal, making AGER. Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagerly means keenly, with enthusiasm, both adverbs.

clue.text: Serious pledge

definitions.meaning: serious here means sincere, solemn in intent
a pledge here means a token deposit given to secure a deal

explanation.definitionFit: Earnest is both a sincere adjective and a noun for money paid as a guarantee.
